general.order_files: a 3D STEP model is required; a 2D drawing (pdf, dwg, dxf) only for threads, silkscreen, welding or tolerances. JLCCNC works from the STEP, so the flat pattern is theirs.
general.k_factor: not published (English or Chinese pages). It affects only qfold's own flat pattern, since JLCCNC unfolds the STEP. The design guide's ranges: mild steel 0.30-0.40, aluminum 0.33-0.50, stainless 0.40-0.50; qfold uses the midpoint.
general.min_flange_rule: half the V-die plus about 2 mm (bending article); the per-thickness table adds margin
general.hole_to_bend: features closer than 3 mm to a bend line distort (bending article); hole edge to bend tangent >= 2 T (design guide)
general.min_hole: at least T/2 and at least 1.0
general.radius_dies: full-arc dies for large radii (R3-R20 on the English page, R5-R40 in the Chinese article)

columns.T_actual: actual sheet thickness for that nominal (Chinese materials article)
columns.R_outer: outer bend corner radius (guidelines article); inside radius is R_outer - T
columns.flange: recommended minimum bend flange (bending article), taken as outside of the other leg to the edge

notes: The minimum flange table is read as an outside dimension (like SendCutSend's): the die shoulder sits half the V-die from the bend's outside apex. The article doesn't say which dimension it means.
0.8 mm is stocked but has no outer radius in the table, so its bend radius is unknown.
Minimum flange is published for 1.0-3.0 mm only; elsewhere qfold uses the article's rule, V/2 + 2 mm with V = 6 T.
